SolarWave is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for customer-facing inference that has strict latency SLOs, on-prem data residency requirements in EMEA, and compliance needs. transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-11-30
- Time: 16:00 PT
- Duration: 46 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Chen (Redwood SE), Rosa Kim (Redwood CSM), Diane Park (SolarWave Head of Platform), Liam O'Connor (SRE), Priya Menon (CISO), Marco Ruiz (Lead ML Eng)

Auto-generated Summary:
SolarWave is building an inference path for embedded product features in its energy monitoring dashboards. They need sub-second 95th pctl latency for common routes, strict data residency for EMEA customers, and an on-prem option for some regulated customers. Discussed fallback topologies (model-variant fallback, region failover, circuit breaker), Dedicated capacity for predictable tail latency, and Private deployment considerations (VPC, KMS/HSM, audit logs).

Topics:
- current infra and where inference will run
- latency/SLOs and QPS expectations
- fallback/failover design (multi-region and canary)
- private/on-prem constraints and KMS/encryption
- compliance and audit logging needs

Action items (auto included in transcript): see metadata

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Patel: hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm maya from redwood, and with me is ethan our se and rosa from csm. um can we do quick intros on the solarwave side?
[00:09] Diane Park: sure, diane here, head of platform. liam is our ops lead, priya's our security owner, marco runs the ml infra.
[00:16] Liam O'Connor (Speaker 1): hey all.
[00:18] Maya Patel: awesome. high level, we hear you're evaluating reliability and also private deploy options. can you walk through the primary constraints and success criteria?
[00:27] Diane Park: yes. So the product team needs the model features to be available in the ui with 95th percentile latency around 300ms or lower for the 90% of traffic. We get spiky bursts (around peak of 200 rps per region) and some long-tail larger prompts.
[00:43] Marco Ruiz: and a few enterprise customers require data to stay in EMEA and one is strictly on-prem airgapped so we need an on-prem option. They also want logs for every request for audit.
[00:54] Priya Menon: security wise, SOC2 is table stakes, but we need KMS with HSM integration, SAML SSO for platform, and detailed audit trails. Also tls everywhere obviously.
[01:05] Ethan Chen: ok that makes sense. quick clarifying q -- is the 300ms target end-to-end or token-latency?
[01:11] Diane Park: it's end-to-end from button click to first token ideally, 95th pctl.
[01:16] Ethan Chen: ok good. that steers us towards Dedicated or Private for tail predictability. Hosted can do fast median but tail gets variable due to multi-tenant noisy neighbors and batching.
[01:26] Maya Patel: right, and we have options for routing policies. we can do active-active multi-region with regional steering, or active-passive with failover. both have tradeoffs for stateful kv cache - say kv cache or kv cash as audio sometimes writes it - but basically the context cache.
[01:41] Liam O'Connor: can you expand on circuit breaker behavior? we want graceful degradation, not a hard stop. some of our routes can tolerate shorter responses, others are critical.
[01:51] Ethan Chen: absolutely. typical pattern we recommend is a per-route circuit breaker with dynamic thresholds: error rate and queue depth triggers. when triggered we first downgrade model to a faster but smaller variant, then switch to cached responses if a prefix cache hits, then finally route to a fallback endpoint which could be a cheaper regional pool or even a canned response.
[02:09] Marco Ruiz: when you say downgrade model, is that automatic? how do you control hallucination risk?
[02:15] Ethan Chen: good question. downgrade is policy-driven; you can limit which prompts are eligible and set confidence thresholds. we also run lightweight rerankers client-side or do quick safety checks. the tradeoff is accuracy vs latency and that's something we'll tune in the pilot.
[02:28] Diane Park: and for the on-prem case, can you do the same fallback matrix inside our datacenter so we don't have to egress data?
[02:34] Maya Patel: for private/on-prem deployments we can run a private control plane and local inference pool. circuit breaker behaviors are supported locally, but for multi-region failover between on-prem and cloud there's extra networking/consistency work and you have to be explicit about what crosses boundaries.
[02:48] Priya Menon: cross-boundary is a NO for some customers. if anything leaves the data center it needs to be encrypted, logged, and have contractual restrictions. we may need a VPC-only path with no outbound internet.
[02:59] Ethan Chen: we support VPC peering and private endpoints; you can opt for a private control plane that never egresses logs offsite. for KMS we integrate with customer-managed keys and HSM providers, though some HSMs in air-gapped sites require an offline key service which complicates rotation.
[03:16] Liam O'Connor: curious about autoscaling. if Dedicated is reserved capacity, how do you handle sudden spikes?
[03:23] Maya Patel: dedicated gives you predictable baseline capacity. we offer burst capacity that can be used for spikes and configurable autoscaling. we also have policies to spill to hosted pools in emergencies but that's opt-in and requires data residency acceptance.
[03:36] Marco Ruiz: what's the SLA for Dedicated? we need uptime and latency SLOs tied to credits/rebates for enterprise.
[03:43] Rosa Kim: our Dedicated plans include SLA for uptime and for tail latency we provide percentile-based SLOs in the contract; the exact numbers and remedies are negotiable based on committed capacity. we can share a sample SLA.
[03:54] Diane Park: another question — how do you handle KV cache warming after failover? we noticed long tails while caches rehydrate in previous vendors.
[04:02] Ethan Chen: good point. we support prefix/KV caching with proactive cache warm strategies: push warmers during failover, maintain a small standby warm cache in passive regions, and prefetching using playback of recent traffic. there is cost tradeoff but it's effective to reduce cold-start penalty.
[04:18] Liam O'Connor: does the cache have to be shared across regions? we worry about cross-region replication and GDPR.
[04:24] Ethan Chen: it doesn't have to be; you can keep region-local caches. when you need cross-region failover, you can configure limited metadata-only replication or use anonymized cache keys to avoid PII. that's configurable per-customer.
[04:37] Priya Menon: audit logs — we need immutable request logs and the ability to export to our SIEM. retention policy will be defined by compliance but we need at least 7 years for some contracts. is that supported?
[04:47] Maya Patel: we can stream audit logs to customer endpoints (S3, GCS, Splunk, etc.) and provide WORM style retention policies via bucket configuration. for private deployments we can route logs to on-prem SIEM.
[04:59] Marco Ruiz: on the security doc front, what's included in your standard pack?
[05:03] Rosa Kim: we'll send our security datasheet: SOC2 report, penetration test summary, network diagrams, encryption-at-rest/in-transit details, KMS integration guide, and our incident response playbook.
[05:13] Diane Park: direct question on latency: can Redwood hit 300ms 95th for our typical prompt size (avg 80 tokens) in Dedicated across eu-west-1?
[05:22] Ethan Chen: with Dedicated and pinned model versions on GPU with optimized kernels we commonly see sub-300ms 95th for that prompt size, assuming correct batching policies and workload shaping. we'll verify in the benchmark.
[05:33] Liam O'Connor: what about tokenization differences and model variants? will that change P95 dramatically?
[05:38] Ethan Chen: model variant and quantization can affect latency. we provide quantization profiles that keep quality loss minimal. we'll include recommended profiles for your workload during the pilot.
[05:47] Maya Patel: cost note — Dedicated baseline vs Hosted: Dedicated gives predictability and lower tail latency but a fixed commit. Hosted is lower upfront but variable cost. We can model both with your 200 rps peak and 100 rps baseline.
[05:59] Diane Park: are there customers that run hybrid: some customers on on-prem, others on hosted?
[06:04] Rosa Kim: yes, hybrid is common. we manage different routing policies per-customer and per-route which lets you keep strict customers on private pools and route the rest to hosted/dedicated.
[06:14] Priya Menon: legal will ask about subprocessors and data flows. we need a list of subprocessors and where data may be routed for failover.
[06:22] Maya Patel: we'll include subprocessors and a map of failover flows in the security packet.
[06:27] Marco Ruiz: operationally, who owns the rollback in an incident? our SRE or Redwood?
[06:31] Ethan Chen: ownership is contract-defined. typical pattern: your SRE triggers canaries and rollbacks via our API or console; we can also set automated fallback rules that run without manual steps. but we can set runbooks where you have final control for certain operations.
[06:46] Lily (Speaker mislabeled): mm, question on demo — can you show the console routing UI in follow-up?
[06:50] Maya Patel: absolutely, ethan can demo the routing and rollout UI and we'll include a canary policy example.
[06:55] Diane Park: timeline wise, we'd like a pilot in january if security checks go well.
[06:58] Maya Patel: sounds good. we'll aim to get the benchmark scheduled and security docs out this week.
[07:04] Ethan Chen: quick note on fallback observability — we surface per-route token counts, model variants used, fallback events, and error rates in the console and you can tie them to alerts.
[07:15] Liam O'Connor: do you provide tracing to link requests end-to-end?
[07:18] Ethan Chen: yes we export traces and integrate with OpenTelemetry so you can link frontend to inference traces.
[07:24] Marco Ruiz: if we opt for private with air-gapped on-prem, what about patching and security updates?
[07:29] Rosa Kim: we provide an update bundle workflow for air-gapped environments; it's a signed bundle that you can apply on a controlled cadence. we also offer a support plan for assisted updates.
[07:39] Diane Park: last thing — can you put together a fallback matrix example that maps route->downgrade->cache->fallback response? that's what engineering wants to see.
[07:47] Maya Patel: yes, we'll include a sample fallback matrix in the follow-up materials and propose default thresholds.
[07:52] Priya Menon: ok thanks.
[07:53] Maya Patel: great. recap then: maya to send pricing worksheet and dedicated diagram, ethan to schedule benchmark and prep plan, rosa to send security pack and sample sla, priya to share security questionnaire and constraints. follow-up scheduled 2026-12-08.
[08:10] Diane Park: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[08:12] Maya Patel: thanks all, bye.
